problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} & \frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} \\ -\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}5 & \sqrt{2} \\ 4\sqrt{2} & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Find $|\text{det}(PQ)|$ given that $P$ is an orthogonal matrix.

feedback.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{37}} & \frac{6}{\sqrt{37}} \\ -\frac{6}{\sqrt{37}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{37}}\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}10 & \sqrt{6} \\ -2\sqrt{6} & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Find $|\text{det}(PQ)|$ given that $P$ is an orthogonal matrix.
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the following facts: 

- The determinant of a product is equal to the product of the determinants.

- The determinant of an orthogonal matrix $P$ is equal to $\pm 1.$

Applying these ideas, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\text{det}(PQ)| & =|\text{det}(P)\cdot \text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|(\pm 1)\cdot \text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|\pm 1|\cdot |\text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|\text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|10\cdot (-1)-\sqrt{6}\cdot (-2\sqrt{6})| \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
